It is evident, then, that in the case of simples there is no inquiry nor teaching, but a different manner of inquiry for such things. —Since that which is compounded out of something in such a way that the whole is one—erefore what we seek is the cause, i.e. the form, by reason of which the matter is some definite thing; and this is the substance of the thing. Evidently, then, in the case of simple terms no inquiry ◀nor teaching is possible; our attitude towards such things is other than that of inquiry.
